01

Artificial intelligence

The current work

Two years of teaching generative tooling to carry an idea from first sketch to finished product without losing the hand that made it. Not prompts typed into somebody else's website — a stack that runs on my own machine, models I have trained myself, and pipelines built to produce the same answer twice.

I came to it as an artist, which is the part that matters. A model will happily give you something plausible and wrong. Knowing which one is which is still the job.

WHERE I STOP

Client material does not go to a third-party service. A real person's likeness does not get generated without their say-so. And nothing ships that I have not looked at frame by frame — a tool that makes a thousand images still needs somebody who can say which one is right.

WHAT RUNS HERE

machine
Apple silicon, local and offline. No upload, no third party, no client data leaving the building.
front ends
ComfyUI, InvokeAI and AUTOMATIC1111 over one shared model library.
image
Flux.1 and Flux.2, SDXL, Qwen-Image, Z-Image, SD 1.5 — chosen per shot, not per habit.
video
Image-to-video and restyle passes, driven shot by shot rather than clip by clip.
training
LoRAs trained on my own reference sheets, so a character stays the same character across hundreds of frames.
tooling
A desktop app I wrote: finds and installs models from Civitai and Hugging Face, queues restyle and video jobs, and keeps the whole kit portable on an external drive.

Renders in minutes, not days

At The Designery I built an AI imaging workflow that turned client visuals around inside a meeting rather than inside a week — and walked clients through the finished room in VR before anything was built.

THE DESIGNERY · 2024—25

A film, restyled frame by frame

Twenty-four minutes of 4:3 standard definition rebuilt as 16:9 at 1080p. Every shot restyled to one consistent look, with an automated gate that catches a pop or a flash at each cut before a frame is signed off.

PERSONAL · IN PROGRESS

R&D inside a regulated programme

Leading AI research and development for learning design at an aircraft manufacturer, where speed is worth nothing if a single published word cannot be traced back to the expert who said it.

CIRRUS AIRCRAFT · 2025—NOW

01 — INTERVIEW What the expert actually said, captured once.
02 — DESIGN One layout, made by hand, that the machine then follows.
03 — GENERATE Models, LoRAs and templates filling it out at volume.

Studio

All six references

I started in 3D in 1998, modelling characters for films that went out on national television. That taught me to think in space before I think in layers — and it is still how I plan a frame, a lesson or a page.

Since then: nine years at Jellyvision turning benefits enrolment into something watchable, a contract month at Jackbox drawing two hundred props, three years at Tynker running graphics for a product children actually used. Different rooms, same job — make the thing clear, then make it worth looking at.

The newest part of the practice is the generative one, and I treat it the way I treated 3D in 1998: learn the machine properly, then use it to do the work I already knew how to do, faster and at a scale I could not reach alone.
